paragraphs: Qing List (qing-bestsellers-top) is an adults-only sales chart for intimate products. It puts public bestseller pages that were open that day, or that week, on one page and keeps the name, price, rating, image, and product link.
The point is comparison. It is not a shop and not a paid placement. To order, go back to the merchant and check stock and price there.
The site is for people aged 18 and over. The pages are about adult intimate products, and you confirm your age before the list is shown.
The chart is not medical or health advice, and it is not a suggestion to buy, use, or switch any product.

sections.h2: What today and this week mean
paragraphs: Today is the public Top 20 for one Shanghai date. This week is the Top 20 for Monday through Sunday in that timezone. The home page opens on today; ?board=weekly opens the week.

Each issue follows its JSON file. If the weekly file has seed, the page says it is a copy of one day. When the same ISO week already has two or more daily files, scripts/build_weekly.py writes an aggregate with no seed. 2026-W42 is that aggregate. How the order is built, and which shops are in, is on Methodology.

Simplified Chinese is the default. The same pages can be read in English, Japanese, or Spanish with ?lang=en, ?lang=ja, or ?lang=es. The URL with no language parameter is Chinese, and it is the hreflang x-default.
青榜友链/合作目录页. Links we may add when directories require a reciprocal. Badges and backlinks for adult directories stay on that one page.
The homepage does not carry an AdultList dofollow link, and reciprocal links are not in the footer of every page. Product links stay nofollow.

method.title: Methodology | sources, updates, and ranking rules
method.description: Where the intimate-product sales chart reads from (Taobao/Tmall, Amazon, independent shops), how often the daily and weekly files update, the ranking rule, and what it cannot claim.
method.ogImageAlt: Qing List methodology for the intimate-product sales chart.
method.kicker: How the chart is built · Adults 18+ only
method.lead: Each issue uses only public pages that were open at the time. No product was invented to fill 20 places, and older dates are not mixed in.

paragraphs: The chart is designed to read three kinds of public pages: Taobao/Tmall, Amazon, and independent or regional shops. Shops that have appeared include Dame, Lovense, We-Vibe, Womanizer, and, in Hong Kong, Waddy, SISTALK, Les'Play, and Sex Concept.
Who is actually in an issue is sources_included in that JSON file. Sources that were not requested, or could not be opened, are listed in sources_skipped. They are not backfilled.

After the earlier 2026-10-16 scrape, three Hong Kong category pages were merged because the static HTML had a product URL, a name, and an HKD price: SISTALK hot-selling, Les'Play best-sellers, and Sex Concept best-sellers. Rank is the top-to-bottom order on that page, at most 6 rows per source, then the existing rule rebuilds the Top 20. Taobao/Tmall the same day returned a JavaScript search shell with no product URL or price, so sources_skipped marks it blocked and no rows were invented. The empty placeholder is data/sources/taobao_tmall.placeholder.json. 18 Gifts' monthly bestseller page was a Cloudflare interstitial. LELO /best-sellers returned 404. MysteryVibe was not retried (HTTP 429 on 2026-10-15). PChome 24h responded, but not as a confirmed bestseller list, so it was not merged.

The daily chart updates once per Asia/Shanghai date. A routine publish replaces data/daily-latest.json in full and writes the same document to data/daily-YYYY-MM-DD.json and data/archive/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Older rows are not merged in.
The weekly chart updates for each Monday–Sunday week in Asia/Shanghai (the ISO week). A routine publish replaces data/weekly-latest.json in full and writes data/archive/weekly/YYYY-Www.json.

The daily file was first written at 2026-10-16T10:59:47+08:00 and rewritten at 2026-10-16T17:03:22+08:00 after the Hong Kong shops were added. Prices and ranks match the date in the file, not live stock at the moment you open the page.

The weekly chart is not meant to stay a copy of one day. scripts/build_weekly.py reads data/archive/daily/. When one ISO week (Asia/Shanghai, Monday–Sunday) has two or more daily files, it dedupes by product URL, ranks by days appeared, mean source rank, and best source rank, and writes data/weekly-latest.json plus data/archive/weekly/YYYY-Www.json with no seed. 2026-W42 uses 2026-10-15, 2026-10-16, 2026-10-17, and 2026-10-18, so it is an aggregate, not a copy. If a week has only one daily, the script leaves the existing weekly file alone. If that file still has seed, the page says it is a copy of that day.

The combined list dedupes by product link, keeps at most six items from each source, then sorts by the shop's own rank (lower first), then rating (higher first; missing ratings last), then review count (higher first; missing counts last), then platform id and name. The first 20 remain.

The same rule is stored in the file as sort_rule: dedupe by product_url; cap 6 per source; sort by source rank ASC, then rating DESC (nulls last), then review count DESC (nulls last), then platform id, then name; take Top 20.
The by-shop page does not rerank. It groups the same 20. The count in parentheses is how many made the combined list, not the full length of that shop's own chart.
These limits apply to every issue. Before reading one, check sources_skipped, omissions, and seed in that file.
items: This is not worldwide sales, and it is not an official Taobao, Tmall, or Amazon master chart.

Only rows that were open and had a product link are kept. A slide with no link (Lush 4 / Lush Mini on the Lovense homepage in the 2026-10-16 daily file) is recorded under omissions and is not in the top 20.
Price, stock, discounts, and rank all move. A figure labeled “As low as” is the starting price shown on that page.

If a weekly JSON has seed, it is a copy of one day's chart, not a separate week-long tally. 2026-W42 has no seed: it is aggregated from the 2026-10-15, 2026-10-16, 2026-10-17, and 2026-10-18 daily files. A week with only one daily may still be a seed.
Outbound links use nofollow. This site does not take payment, ship orders, or give medical or health advice, and it does not decide a purchase for you.

privacy.title: Privacy | Qing List
privacy.description: Qing List is a static adults-only site. This page covers Google Analytics 4 (G-1SF9TQS3F1), the age and language choices stored in the browser, no sale of personal data, and outbound shop links.
privacy.ogImageAlt: Qing List privacy policy. Adults 18+ only.
privacy.kicker: Adults-only site · no sale of personal data
privacy.lead: Qing List does not sell products and has no accounts. This page only describes data the site actually touches.

paragraphs: Qing List is a static GitHub Pages chart of public intimate-product bestsellers for adults 18 and older. There is no registration, cart, payment, or shipping.
Product buttons leave this site for the merchant. Those sites have their own privacy policies.
Before entering, you confirm you are 18 or older. That choice stays in your browser's localStorage under qbt-age. Language stays under qbt-lang.
Neither value is uploaded to a Qing List server. There is no backend and no profile that can be looked up by name.
Pages use Google Analytics 4, measurement ID G-1SF9TQS3F1. It may record page views, approximate region, device, and referrer through cookies, so we can see which charts are opened.
That measurement is not sold as an advertising profile and is not handed to merchants as a visitor list. You can limit third-party cookies or block Google Analytics in the browser.
Personal data is not sold, traded, or rented. There is no member list and no checkout record to sell.
Product links go to Amazon, brand sites, or Hong Kong shops and use nofollow. Cookies, accounts, and orders after that belong to the other site.
Pages are for adults 18 and older. Do not give this site to minors. The charts are not medical advice.
A static site cannot delete a profile it does not have. To correct a product row, or to ask about this policy, use the GitHub issues link on the contact page.
